PCI.text: Physical Cell Identity (0-503): the number a phone reads from a cell's sync signals to tell neighbouring cells apart. Not unique worldwide, only nearby.

TAC.text: Tracking Area Code: cells are grouped into tracking areas. An idle phone only tells the network when it enters a different area.

EARFCN.text: E-UTRA Absolute Radio Frequency Channel Number: the channel a cell transmits on. It fixes the band and the exact frequency.

ECI.text: E-UTRAN Cell Identity: eNB ID (top 20 bits) plus cell ID (bottom 8 bits). Unique within the operator's network.

eNB ID.text: Identifies the base station (eNodeB). One eNB can serve several cells.

A3.text: Measurement event A3: a neighbour becomes better than the serving cell by an offset. The phone reports it and the eNB decides on a handover.

hysteresis.text: Extra margin on top of the A3 offset, so a phone at the border does not hand over back and forth.

time to trigger.text: How long the A3 condition must hold (in radio time) before the phone reports it.

AMBR.text: Aggregate Maximum Bit Rate: the subscriber's speed limit (the plan), per direction.

IMSI.text: International Mobile Subscriber Identity: the SIM's identity. MCC (country) + MNC (operator) + subscriber number.

PLMN.text: Public Land Mobile Network: an operator's network, written as MCC-MNC (here 999-70, a test code).

APN.text: Access Point Name: which data network the phone asks for (here 'internet').

connected.text: RRC connected: the phone has a radio connection to a cell right now and can send data immediately. Without traffic the eNB releases it after a while (idle).

idle.text: RRC idle: the phone is attached (it has an IP) but has no radio connection. The first packet wakes it up with a Service Request.

S1.text: The interface between an eNB and the core: S1-MME (signalling, SCTP) and S1-U (user data, GTP-U).

GTP.text: GPRS Tunnelling Protocol: user packets travel between the eNB and the core inside GTP-U tunnels; a handover moves the tunnel to the new eNB.

PRB.text: Physical Resource Block: 12 subcarriers. The number of PRBs sets a cell's bandwidth (25 PRB = 5 MHz).

roaming.text: Using another operator's network with your own SIM. The visited network asks your home network to authenticate you.
